meaning.zh:
“脱离困境” 或 “摆脱危险”。

这个短语的起源可以追溯到古老的欧洲，在那时候，穿越森林常常是危险且不确定的。当人们说他们已经 “out of the woods”，意味着他们已经穿越了危险地带，进入了相对安全的地方。在现代社会，这个短语用来比喻任何一种困境或挑战，表示走出困境或者危险时期。
meaning.en: This phrase dates back to ancient Europe, where traversing woods was often dangerous and uncertain. When people said they were "out of the woods," it meant they had traversed a dangerous area and reached a relatively safer place. In contemporary usage, the phrase metaphorically refers to any kind of trouble or challenge, indicating that one has emerged from a difficult or dangerous period.

lines.en: After months of treatment, the doctors finally said he was *out of the woods*.
lines.zh: 经过几个月的治疗，医生终于说他脱离了危险。

lines.en: The company was *out of the woods* after a year of financial troubles.
lines.zh: 经历了一年的财务困境后，公司终于脱离了困境。

lines.en: We are not yet *out of the woods* with this project, but things are improving.
lines.zh: 在这个项目上我们尚未摆脱困境，但情况正在好转。
